description: Held-back structural causal model for the workplace-wellbeing enrollment ATE task. Enrollment is driven by a strong administrative process count (outreach_contacts) that has no direct effect on the wellbeing index, by several linear baseline covariates, by tenure_years, and by two mean-zero three-way products of sines among disjoint baseline covariate triples that also enter the outcome and therefore confound. outreach_contacts is a near-instrument: conditioning on it amplifies the residual bias left when the oscillatory confounders are not modeled. The treatment effect is heterogeneous in tenure_years, whose mean is well away from zero, so the population average effect equals tau + tau_het*mean(tenure_years). Recovering it needs both oscillatory terms reconstructed from the baseline covariates at their own frequencies, the eight linear baselines and tenure adjusted for, outreach_contacts left out, and the enrolled-minus-not contrast averaged over every employee. All confounding is through measured covariates, so the effect is point identified.
